messages:
riley: hi all, quickstart CLI failure. ran `npx @redwood/cli init` then `redwood quickstart run` and first API call returns 403: 'onboarding_blocked:billing_missing'.
morgan_dev: can you paste the CLI command and the error body? which quickstart (node/python)?
riley: node quickstart. cli command was `REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx redwood quickstart run --example chat`
error printed by CLI:
```
Request failed: 403
{"error":"onboarding_blocked","reason":"billing_missing","hint":"add billing to activate API"}
```
anya_support: thanks. this is the new onboarding gate that blocks API access until billing/TOS are confirmed. CLI should surface a clearer action instead of raw JSON.
jamie_sdk: agreed. parity gap: Go and Python SDKs already translate 'onboarding_blocked' to a typed OnboardingError with instructions; Node CLI currently just prints raw response. I'll file DEVEX-1501 to add a user-friendly message and a docs link.
riley: another ask: for local dev it's pretty annoying to add a card just to try the sample. is there a recommended dev flow?
anya_support: short-term: we can issue ephemeral sandbox tokens via support, but that requires manual step. long-term: thinking about a CLI preflight that detects onboarding state and prints next steps.
morgan_dev: idea: add a `--allow-sandbox` flag to `redwood quickstart run` that uses an internal sandbox mode when `REDWOOD_SANDBOX=true`. This would switch endpoints to sandbox.redwood.ai and not enforce billing gates.
security: heads up: we need to be careful exposing a sandbox bypass. sandbox infrastructure must be rate-limited and isolated. we cannot allow a simple env var to bypass hosted protections. any bypass needs to be bound to a sandbox account issued by support.
jamie_sdk: what if the CLI supports `--sandbox-token <token>` which we can issue via support or via an automated ephemeral token endpoint (auth: support app)? then no silent bypass. CLI can detect absence of token and suggest contacting support.
anya_support: that sounds reasonable. support can offer a one-click sandbox token for new users that lasts 24h. will scope a small effort.
morgan_dev: implementation plan for CLI: 1) add preflight call GET /orgs/:id/status or GET /auth/whoami to check onboarding state. 2) if blocked, print clear steps and a `--sandbox-token` example. 3) update quickstart README.
riley: that would be perfect. preflight would have saved me a lot of time. also can we add a retry suggestion for membership propagation issues? sometimes I accept invite and first call fails.
jamie_sdk: (jamie) yes — will also include special-casing for membership propagation errors (`membership_pending`) and recommend "retry after 30s" with exponential backoff helper in the CLI. filing DEVEX-1501 and DEVEX-1502.
security: please ensure sandbox-token usage is logged and sandbox endpoints are separated. I'll review the design.
anya_support: i'll draft a short support KB and a canned response for onboarding-blocked cases, plus a process for issuing sandbox tokens.
morgan_dev: i'll open a small PR to change the CLI output to something like:
```
Onboarding blocked: add billing or accept TOS to enable API access.
If you're trying out the quickstart, request a sandbox token from support or run:
REDWOOD_SANDBOX_TOKEN=<token> redwood quickstart run --sandbox-token
See https://docs.redwood.ai/onboarding for details.
```
riley: thanks everyone. please ping me on the PR, i'll validate the UX. saved a lot of confusion. :relieved:
